newsitem.title: USA: Conn. panel rejects Woody Allen's complaint.
newsitem.headline: Conn. panel rejects Woody Allen's complaint.

text.p: A Connecticut grievance panel Wednesday recommended dismissing a complaint by film director Woody Allen against a state's attorney who investigated allegations of child abuse against Allen.
A subcommittee of the Statewide Grievance Committee, a lawyers' disciplinary group, recommended that Allen's complaints against Litchfield County state's attorney Frank Maco be dropped.
The proposal now goes to the full, 15-member committee.
Allen claimed that Maco damaged his reputation in 1993 when Maco said there was enough evidence to prosecute Allen on charges of molesting his daughter, but that Maco would not pursue the case.
The charges were brought by actress Mia Farrow, and involved the couple's adopted daughter, Dylan.
Maco told Reuters that the episode was "an ordeal" and that he felt relieved.
"This is the third complaint that's been entertained by Mr. Allen in this state," he said.
"I feel their decision recognised the situation in which I found myself in September 1993 ... with such a high-profile, high-visibility case."
Maco said he hoped the decision would finally close the book on the dispute.
Allen and Farrow's relationship soured in January 1992, when Farrow found photographs of her adopted daughter, Soon-Yi Previn, posing naked in Allen's New York City apartment.
In August 1992, Allen was accused of molesting and sexually assaulting his 7-year-old adopted daughter at Farrow's home in Bridgewater, Conn.
The complaint was initially filed with New York authorities, but Connecticut later became involved.
Allen, 61, has vehemently denied the child abuse charges.
